items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: he was the manager of a USO show that went overseas -- and I was with the band; I was with his show.

ctx.x: Sylvester Lewis was his name. He was very much a part of Claude Hopkins' band, you know. And down through the war years, the broke up, he came out of Claude's band, and he was the manager of a USO show that went overseas -- and I was with the band; I was with his show. Oh, we had a wonderful trip over there. It was only... We were there six months. But it was wonderful. And he was a really good manager.

Well, he stopped playing his horn... After he came back, he stopped playing his horn altogether, and he got a job in the subway. He was working in the subway. He had been working there for years, you know. And one day him and I, we had a... He had a gig, he had a little dance to play, and at that time I had got my first tape recorder. So I came with the tape recorder on the job. And it was his band, you know. And I taped it on the job.

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: No, it wasn't O.B. Sylvester Lewis.

ctx.x: No, it wasn't O.B. Sylvester Lewis.
